Turkish Renewable Energy Workers Walk Out, Halting Projects Nationwide

A major walkout by workers in Turkey’s renewable energy industry has brought development and operations to a standstill across much of the sector. The industrial action, which began early Monday, saw thousands of staff from wind, solar and geothermal plants down tools, demanding improved wages and safety measures.

The strike is affecting both ongoing construction sites and operational facilities. At the 200-MW Suryel Solar Park in Konya province, assembly lines and maintenance teams have stopped work, leaving panels idle. “Our members are committed to sustainable energy, but they can’t accept unsafe working conditions and stagnant pay,” said Emre Aykan, spokesperson for the Federation of Renewable Energy Workers, which organized the strike.

Industry sources estimate that more than 60 percent of projects are currently affected, including several high-profile wind farm expansions along the Aegean coast. “Even routine maintenance is on hold. Output has dropped sharply in the last 48 hours,” said Aylin Koca, chief analyst at Anatolia Renewables Consultancy.

Executives at leading firms, such as Turkuaz Enerji and SolForte, have urged a swift resolution. “We respect workers’ rights and are open to further dialogue, but project delays risk jeopardizing critical investment timelines,” said a Turkuaz Enerji representative.

Analysts warn that an extended stoppage could stall Turkey’s ambitious renewable capacity targets. According to the Turkish Renewable Power Association, the sector employs over 30,000 people directly. “This is a pivotal moment,” said association president Selim Gündoğan. “A prolonged disruption could have lasting consequences for the industry’s growth trajectory.”

Negotiations between union representatives and company officials are scheduled to resume later this week. For now, most sites remain quiet as the walkout continues.
